source.title: Alignment among Language, Vision and Action Representations

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It contains some apparent naming and formatting inconsistencies, but these do not prevent extraction of the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: It measures cross-model representational alignment with P@k and orthogonal Procrustes, rather than testing convergence as model scale or capability increases.
record.gate_note: The study compares action-language embeddings with language and vision-language model embeddings for the same 108 BabyAI instructions. It varies P@k and also reports Procrustes results. It does not test model scaling, paired image-caption alignment as model capability increases, seed-to-seed shared features, universal features, or causal explanations for alignment. Prior-work results cited in the paper and task-solving rates are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: It measures, in a new embodied-action setting, how well a small behaviour-cloned action-language model aligns with pretrained LLM and VLM text embeddings of 108 BabyAI instructions. It uses mutual-neighbour P@k, close to PRH's mutual-kNN, plus orthogonal Procrustes. There is no scale or capability sweep, so the results bear on partial convergence (V7), metric dependence (V6) and mapping quality (V4), not on scaling (V1).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the authors frame the result more strongly than the record does. They call the alignment robust and surprisingly high, and say ALM–decoder-LLM alignment approaches LLM–LLM alignment. They also report that CLIP and BERT align much less. They read this as evidence for modality-independent semantic organisation and potential cross-domain transfer. They caveat that the instruction set is restricted, the environment simplified, and geometric measures do not show functional equivalence.
record.recipe_differences: Uses P@k nearest-neighbor overlap and orthogonal Procrustes on 108 BabyAI instructions, comparing action-trained embeddings with pretrained model embeddings. The text does not describe a reproduction of either original source's method; it introduces action representations as the additional setting.
record.method_sensitivity: P@k depends on k (1, 5, 10, 15); alignment also differs across model and metric. Inputs are restricted to 108 instructions from the BabyAI vocabulary; no alternate or out-of-distribution input set is tested.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed and unvaried scale, a small action-only behaviour-cloned model's instruction embeddings share nearest-neighbour structure with LLM and BLIP text embeddings. P@15 is 0.66–0.70 against random 0.13; alignment with CLIP and BERT is weaker (0.31–0.35).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models trained on different objectives and modalities (including embodied action) converge on shared relational structure over the same inputs, independent of any scale trend.

record.problems: One simulated environment and a restricted set of 108 linguistically simple instructions; the paper itself says these limit linguistic diversity and semantic richness. Action representations come from a single simplified setting. Procrustes results are described largely with approximate grouped medians rather than individual numerical values. Geometric alignment does not directly test functional equivalence or causal grounding. No scaling or out-of-distribution analysis.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results left out. Individual model-pair P@15 values among decoder-only LLMs are not stated; the reported aggregate range is recorded in p15-llm-pairs.

untested.parts: No model size or capability sweep; the relation of alignment to scale is not tested.
Only text encoders of CLIP/BLIP are used. No paired image–caption alignment, and no relation to capability.
There are 10 ALM seeds, but ALM–ALM alignment across seeds is not reported.
Untested: held-out mapping evaluation, general linear maps, stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, and downstream functional loss.
No feature, neuron or circuit analysis.
Input set not varied; no out-of-distribution inputs; no comparison with other kernel measures such as CKA or RSA.
No test of plateau with scale, or of whether shared data or objectives cause the alignment.

missing.what: Full pairwise P@15 heatmap among all seven models plus random, e.g. BLIP–CLIP, BERT–LLMs, VLM–LLM pairs. Only the LLM–LLM range is recorded.
Permutation test: all non-random P@15 alignments are above chance (p<0.001, 1000 permutations).
Per-model Procrustes median disparities (only grouped approximate ranges are given in the text).

record.verdict_notes: Reported numbers are inconsistent within the paper. The abstract and Results give ALM–decoder-LLM P@15 of 0.70–0.73, but Table 1 gives 0.68–0.70 and BLIP 0.66. The Discussion gives P@k 0.49–0.67. The 'order of magnitude above random at P@1' claim fails for CLIP. Procrustes is fit and scored on the same 108 points, with PCA to match dimensions. LLM sizes are not stated, and the DeepSeek citation (R1) conflicts with the stated 800B-token corpus. Higher LLM–LLM alignment ('trained on the same task') is consistent with V7's shared-objective explanation, but it is not tested causally. Tranche changed from T2 to T3: the setting (action-trained model) is new, and P@k is close to PRH's mutual-kNN metric.

versions.untested_parts: No model size or capability sweep, and no test of whether cross-model alignment rises with size or capability.

The study compares text-instruction embeddings, including text encoders from vision-language models; it does not compare representations of paired images and captions or relate alignment to both models' capability.
Although the action model has 10 random initializations, the study does not report alignment or shared features between those initializations.

Tests orthogonal Procrustes alignment of the action model with other models on one instruction set. Does not test stitching, relative representations as a transfer method, unpaired mapping, or functional loss after mapping.
No interpretable feature, neuron, SAE feature, or circuit recurrence analysis.
Varies P@k and reports Procrustes as another geometric measure. Does not vary the input set or test out-of-distribution inputs; the tested instructions come from one closed BabyAI vocabulary.
Reports incomplete and model-dependent alignment. Does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause the alignment, or whether alignment plateaus as models scale.

relationships.condition: ALM vs all six pretrained models, P@15 and Procrustes on 108 BabyAI instructions
relationships.reason: Alignment is incomplete throughout. ALM–model P@15 is 0.31–0.70, below the 0.83–0.93 seen among LLMs (p15-*, p15-llm-pairs). The best Procrustes disparity is still about 0.75–0.80 against a random 1.0 (proc-llms).
relationships.display_finding: ALM–model P@15 was 0.31–0.70 versus 0.83–0.93 among LLMs, and the best Procrustes disparity remained about 0.75–0.80 versus a random baseline of 1.0.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Choice of metric (P@k vs orthogonal Procrustes), BLIP and BERT
source_check.reason: BLIP provides the metric-dependent contrast: P@15=0.6598 places it near decoder LLMs, while median Procrustes disparity exceeds 0.85. BERT is comparatively weak under both measures.

relationships.reason: Model ordering (decoder LLMs and BLIP above BERT and CLIP) is stable across k, and all models except CLIP at k=1 stay well above random. The rise with k mostly mirrors the random baseline (0.0056 to 0.1312). The k setting does not overturn the result (p1-* to p15-*).
relationships.display_finding: Decoder LLMs and BLIP consistently ranked above BERT and CLIP, with all models except CLIP at k=1 well above random; increasing alignment largely tracked the random baseline rising from 0.0056 to 0.1312.
